_meta.note: The next 5 how-tos — the adoption on-ramp completing hero journeys 1 (prompt loop -> controlled project) and 3 (model dependency -> worker neutrality). Same dogfooded discipline: runnable proof per claim + adversarial refutation. All proofs are DETERMINISTIC: the two backend guides mock the model/CLI (a canned local HTTP server for Ollama; a stub `claude` on PATH) so the REAL adapter+driver+gate path is exercised without a live model. Q0: a full init->author->drive->gate->done cycle. DA0: a worked-example DAG is lint+audit clean and runs, and a prompt-shaped/hollow DAG is rejected by the auditor. SR0: kill and resume — completed work survives from the event log (state.json is disposable) and the tick continues from the next task, not a redo. OL0: drive the real ollama backend against a mock server end-to-end to a passing gate. CC0: drive the real claude-code adapter with a stub claude to a passing gate, and confirm it degrades when claude is absent. DW0: the five guides + index + suite enforcement (T59). Each proof carries a negative/silent control.

tasks.title: Write quickstart-e2e.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/quickstart-e2e.sh: run the exact 5-minute flow — hb init, author a minimal one-phase DAG with a behavioral gate, drive it with a deterministic script backend that produces the artifact, and assert the phase completes (completed_phases includes it, the gate passed). Control: with a backend that does NOT produce the artifact, the phase does NOT complete (so completion is real). Print QUICKSTART-OK only when the full cycle completes.

phases.title: Turn a plan into a DAG

tasks.title: Write dag-authoring-check.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/dag-authoring-check.sh: a worked-example DAG (phases -> tasks -> a behavioral gate) is lint-clean AND audit-clean AND runs green under a deterministic script backend; and a common-mistake DAG — a prompt-shaped one whose gate is hollow (test -f / true) — is REJECTED by hb-audit (hollow_gate). Print DAG-AUTHORING-OK only when the good DAG is clean and runnable and the bad DAG is caught.

tasks.title: Write stop-resume.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/stop-resume.sh: a two-phase project; complete phase 1; simulate a dead session by deleting state.json (the projection); resume by rebuilding from the event log and assert phase 1 is STILL completed (state comes from events, not memory) and the tick now points to phase 2's task (it continues, it does not redo phase 1). Control: before resume, deleting state.json loses the projection; rebuild restores it identically. Print STOP-RESUME-OK only when the completed work survives and the run continues from the next task.

tasks.title: Write ollama-backend.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/ollama-backend.sh: stand up a local mock Ollama server (a canned /api/generate returning a FILE-block) on an OS-assigned port, drive the REAL ollama backend via hb exec run against it, and assert the artifact is written and the phase's behavioral gate passes (deterministic — the model is mocked, the adapter+driver+gate path is real). Control: pointed at a dead host the backend degrades and the phase does not complete. Print OLLAMA-BACKEND-OK only when the mock-driven run completes.

tasks.title: Write claude-backend.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/claude-backend.sh: put a stub `claude` on PATH that produces the artifact and exits 0, drive the REAL claude-code adapter via hb exec run, and assert the phase completes through its behavioral gate (deterministic — the CLI is mocked, the adapter+driver+gate path is real). Control: with no claude on PATH the adapter degrades to a protocol-valid failure and the phase does NOT complete (escalates). Print CLAUDE-BACKEND-OK only when the stub-driven run completes and the degrade control holds.

tasks.title: Write the journey-1 guides
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/heartbeat-in-5-minutes.md (proof: quickstart-e2e.sh), docs/howto/turn-a-plan-into-a-dag.md (proof: dag-authoring-check.sh), and docs/howto/stop-and-resume-a-project.md (proof: stop-resume.sh). Human-facing, current-state; link the concept ([heartbeat.md]) and the gates guide rather than restating them.

tasks.title: Write the backend guides

tasks.title: Index + enforce
tasks.description: Add the five guides to docs/howto/README.md and flip their rows in docs/howto/howto-list.md from Not-available-yet to the file; add a T59 group to tests/run-tests.sh running quickstart-e2e.sh, dag-authoring-check.sh, stop-resume.sh, ollama-backend.sh, and claude-backend.sh and asserting their markers, so the proofs cannot rot.

review.prompt: Refute that Q0 is done: does it drive the REAL runtime end-to-end (init, a real DAG, a real gate)? Is completion asserted on completed_phases (the gate passing), not just the task running? Is the no-artifact control load-bearing (a backend that doesn't produce the artifact fails to complete)? Could it pass vacuously?

GATE_DA0.desc: A worked-example DAG is clean and runnable; a hollow/prompt-shaped DAG is rejected.

review.prompt: Refute that DA0 is done: is the good DAG genuinely lint- AND audit-clean AND does it actually run to completion (not just validate)? Is the bad DAG genuinely rejected by the auditor for the RIGHT reason (hollow_gate), demonstrating the transformation quality? Could either check be vacuous?

GATE_SR0.desc: Completed work survives a dead session via the event log; the run continues from the next task.

review.prompt: Refute that SR0 is done: does it drive the real CLI? Is the 'kill' real (state.json removed) and does resume genuinely reconstruct completed phase 1 from events (not from a leftover projection)? Does the tick after resume point to phase 2's task (continue), not re-run phase 1? Is the survival load-bearing (would it fail if rebuild lost the completed phase)?

GATE_OL0.desc: The real ollama backend drives a task to a passing gate against a mock server; degrades on a dead host.

review.prompt: Refute that OL0 is done: does it drive the REAL ollama backend (not a reimplementation)? Is the mock server a stand-in only for the MODEL (the HTTP/parse/write/gate path is the real adapter)? Does the phase genuinely complete via its behavioral gate? Is the dead-host degrade control load-bearing (the phase does NOT complete)? Is the port handling deterministic (no fixed-port flakiness)?

GATE_CC0.desc: The real claude-code adapter drives a task to a passing gate with a stub CLI; degrades when claude is absent.

review.prompt: Refute that CC0 is done: does it drive the REAL claude-code adapter (the stub only stands in for the `claude` CLI)? Does the phase complete through its behavioral gate with the stub present? Is the degrade control load-bearing — with no claude on PATH does the adapter emit a protocol-valid failure and the phase NOT complete? Could it pass vacuously?

GATE_DW0.desc: Each guide points at a proof that runs; the index and roadmap list all five; the suite enforces the demos.

review.prompt: Refute that DW0 is done: does any guide claim a proof that does not run? Does any restate the enforced mechanisms rather than link them? Are all five guides in the index AND flipped in howto-list.md? Does T59 actually run all five demos and assert their markers?
